chapter_title: The Five-Level Model of Intelligent Textbooks
learning_objective: The learner will apply the level-specific policy by choosing the lowest level at which each of eight safeguards should first be required, correctly matching at least seven of eight on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** level-specific-safeguard-matcher
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** apply
**Learning Objective:** The learner will apply the level-specific policy by choosing the lowest level at which each of eight safeguards should first be required, correctly matching at least seven of eight on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** the five levels, level-specific policy, graduated regulation (all defined in the chapter sections above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of 8 safeguards, the learner chooses a level from 1 to 5 and submits it. A choice is correct when it equals the "First required at" level in Content. Mastery is 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the level definitions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) All safeguards should apply at every level from the start. (2) Privacy review is needed only for chatbots. (3) A product with no AI model needs no data governance. **Instructional Rationale:** Applying a graduated policy means matching a risk to the capability that first creates it. Items such as the privacy review, which first applies to a product with no AI model, force the learner to link safeguards to capability, not to the amount of AI. **Content:** Eight safeguards: | # | Safeguard shown to the learner | First required at | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Accessibility check of every page for screen readers and keyboard use | 1 | Every student must be able to use any textbook, whatever its level. | | 2 | Independent accuracy check of the simulations by a subject expert | 2 | Interactive models first appear at Level 2 and can mislead if they are wrong. | | 3 | Review of how student records are stored, who sees them, and when they are deleted | 3 | Level 3 is the first level that keeps records about individual students. | | 4 | Parent notice and consent process for collecting student learning data | 3 | Collecting individual learning data begins at Level 3. | | 5 | Bias audit of how the system chooses next steps for different groups of students | 3 | The system first makes individualized choices at Level 3. | | 6 | Hint-first rules and weekly review of the chat tutor's logs | 4 | Open conversation first appears at Level 4. | | 7 | Age limit and supervision rules for open-ended chat | 4 | Open conversation with minors first appears at Level 4. | | 8 | Human review of AI-generated lessons before students see them | 5 | Content is first generated without an author's prior review at Level 5. | **Provenance:** The safeguards and levels follow the chapter section "Graduated Regulation and Level-Specific Policy" and are recommended practice written for this book, not legal requirements. The sim must say so. **Rules:** Each safeguard has exactly one correct first-required level, given in Content. A safeguard is scored on its first submitted choice only. The score counts first-attempt correct choices out of 8. Mastery is a score >= 7. After each answer the sim states that the safeguard also applies to every higher level. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one safeguard at a time and the five levels. 2. The learner chooses the lowest level at which it should first be required and submits. The sim marks it and shows the feedback text. 3. If incorrect, the learner may choose again; the second attempt does not change the score. After the second attempt, the correct level and reason are shown. 4. After all 8, the sim shows the score and a stacked view of the safeguards required at each level. 5. The learner should notice that three safeguards first apply at Level 3, more than at any other level, and that none depends on whether a product contains an AI model. **Feedback:** 8 safeguards, shuffled once per session, two attempts each. Correct: "Correct: Level [n]. [Why text]." Incorrect: "Not quite. [Why text for the correct answer, without naming the level]." After the second attempt the correct level is revealed and the item counts as missed. A running score "First-try correct: n of 8" is shown. Final message for a score >= 7: "You can match safeguards to levels." For a score < 7: "Review where each risk first appears and try again." **Starting State:** Safeguard 1 of the shuffled order is shown with the five levels, the score "First-try correct: 0 of 8," and the prompt "At what level should this first be required?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's safeguard table lists the same eight safeguards at levels 1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, and 5. The chapter states that each safeguard keeps applying at higher levels. The mastery bar is 7 of 8.
